title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: detect sensitivity labels on files inside archives
summary: Hold: the Windows Server support statement omits Microsoft's restrictions and the requirement to enable Endpoint DLP after onboarding. The roadmap dates, general licensing, portal path and PowerShell call are supported; the action rating and governance checklist need minor corrections.

claims.where: controls[0].governs, scope; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: Centrally configured Endpoint DLP settings apply to all DLP policies for devices.
claims.quote: Centrally configured settings control many aspects of endpoint data loss prevention (DLP) behavior. These settings apply to all DLP policies for devices.

claims.claim: In the Microsoft Purview portal, Endpoint settings are reached through Data loss prevention > Overview > Data loss prevention settings > Endpoint settings.
claims.quote: To access these settings, from the Microsoft Purview portal, go to Data loss prevention > Overview > Data loss prevention settings > Endpoint settings.

claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig -EndpointDlpGlobalSettings <PswsHashtable[]> modifies organization-wide endpoint restrictions.
claims.quote: Use the Set-PolicyConfig cmdlet to modify the endpoint restrictions that are configured in the organization. ... [-EndpointDlpGlobalSettings <PswsHashtable[]>]

claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig runs only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: No documented Endpoint setting specifically switches or configures sensitivity-label detection inside archives.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP archive sensitivity label detection Disable classification Set-PolicyConfig EndpointDlpGlobalSettings. Read dlp-configure-endpoint-settings and set-policyconfig, searching archive and sensitivity; no archive-label-specific setting found.

claims.claim: Disable classification excludes monitored file extensions from content scanning.
claims.quote: For files that are on the Monitored files list, you can disable classification through this setting. When you add a file extension to this setting, Endpoint DLP doesn't scan content in files with this extension.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented the effect of Disable classification on this planned archive label detection change.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP archive sensitivity label detection Disable classification Set-PolicyConfig EndpointDlpGlobalSettings. Read dlp-configure-endpoint-settings, including Disable classification, and endpoint-dlp-learn-about; neither explains this planned interaction.

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisite; Scope: Who is affected; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Devices must be onboarded to Microsoft Purview to use them as locations in Endpoint DLP policies.
claims.quote: You need to onboard all the devices you want to use as locations in your DLP policies.

claims.claim: Configuring Endpoint DLP settings and device policies requires the existing Purview permissions for those tasks.
claims.quote: The account you use to create and deploy policies must be a member of one of these role groups: Compliance administrator; Compliance data administrator; Information Protection; Information Protection Admin; Security administrator
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-deploy-policy to sources for the device-policy permissions statement. The already cited Set-PolicyConfig reference separately states that permissions must be assigned to configure endpoint restrictions.

claims.claim: The prepare action rating fits a medium-risk change to existing behaviour with a December 2026 preview target.
claims.quote: action: "prepare"; risk: "medium"; previewDate: "December CY2026"; 'classification and enforcement of archives change'
claims.fix: Set action to 'act-now': the December preview target is within about 60 days of 2026-11-23, the record describes changed existing behaviour, and the briefing already identifies policy-review and communication decisions to take before it lands.
